profiles.meeting_scenario: A 30-minute coordination meeting between the distributed training workstream and the partitioning workstream on a sparse DNN project preparing a final 256-GPU experiment batch for a conference submission. The project trains pruned multilayer networks using SGD implemented as consecutive distributed SpMVs, with row-wise weight partitioning refined by a hypergraph model to cut communication while keeping work balanced. The immediate agenda is to align on the exact partition handoff for the 256-GPU launch, confirm whether the partition is within the target needed to proceed, verify what the 'latest baseline' comparison refers to, and clarify how results from the run will be entered into the team's shared artifact, the Master Results Sheet. The expected outcome is that both participants leave believing they have a clean handoff path, a green light to run, a shared comparison point, and an understood division of responsibility for experiment records.

members.name: Leah Kim
members.expertise: Distributed sparse training systems, GPU communication pipelines, large-scale SGD benchmarking
members.background: Leah owns the end-to-end sparse DNN training stack, including launcher configuration, runtime ingestion of per-layer sparse artifacts, and the benchmark workflow used for paper figures.
members.private_state: She wants this meeting to remove any ambiguity so her team can use the reserved cluster window without needing another round of conversion or bookkeeping work, and she is quietly worried that small interface mismatches will consume the only overnight slot before the internal paper deadline.
hidden_assumptions: A 'partition file' means the exact runtime-consumable artifact the launcher reads for each layer, with row ownership already materialized in the per-rank format used by the distributed SpMV code.
If someone says the partition is 'within target' or 'good to go,' that means it should not create visible per-rank step-time skew in the actual training run, not just in an offline objective.
The 'latest baseline' naturally means the post-pruning-freeze September export that matches the current training branch and mask layout used in recent scaling runs.

The Master Results Sheet is the experiment-of-record, so updating it includes provenance details such as code commit, partition checksum, reservation ID, and any preprocessing path that affected the run.
When a handoff is described as ready for a scheduled run, it is assumed to be directly usable by the execution stack rather than requiring an extra reconstruction step on her side.

members.name: Arjun Narayanan
members.expertise: Hypergraph partitioning, sparse matrix distribution, irregular workload balancing for HPC applications
members.background: Arjun developed the hypergraph-based partitioning formulation and evaluates sparse DNN partitions primarily through offline partition-quality analyses, communication models, and ablation tables rather than through the full training launcher.
members.private_state: He wants the partitioning contribution to remain methodologically clean for the paper and is trying to avoid spending time on packaging details that feel downstream of his main research deliverable, especially while he is still polishing comparative tables.
hidden_assumptions: A 'partition file' is the partition assignment plus enough mapping metadata for another component to reconstruct the row distribution, because that is the standard artifact produced by his toolchain.

If the partition is 'within target' or 'meets the tolerance,' that means it satisfies the imbalance bound in the partitioner's cost model and communication objective, which he treats as the accepted readiness criterion.
The 'latest baseline' refers to the August sparse export and accompanying benchmark input snapshot that underlies his most up-to-date partition analysis tables.

The Master Results Sheet is a top-line summary board for throughput and communication outcomes, while detailed provenance for partition generation belongs in the partition stats directory or local notes.
A coordinated handoff for a run still allows a light conversion step by the systems side, because raw partition outputs are routinely adapted before execution in research prototypes.

misalignment_points.topic: What exactly counts as the partition handoff
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Arjun will send 'the partition files' for the 256-GPU run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Leah believes she will receive per-layer, runtime-ready files already converted into the row-wise ownership format that the launcher and distributed SpMV pipeline directly ingest.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun believes he will send the raw hypergraph partition assignment and associated index/mapping files, expecting Leah's side to do the final conversion into runtime layout.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both regularly refer to exchanged artifacts as 'partition files,' and because previous conversions happened informally without becoming a meeting topic, the phrase sounds precise enough even though it hides a difference in execution assumptions.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means for the partition to be within target
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the current partition is 'within target' or 'good to go' for the large run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Leah takes this to mean the partition should keep observed training-step work sufficiently even across ranks in practice, especially avoiding noticeable skew during forward and backward SpMV on 256 GPUs.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun takes this to mean the partition satisfies the imbalance tolerance in his offline hypergraph objective and communication-volume model, regardless of whether runtime kernel behavior introduces additional skew.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The conversation uses readiness language like 'within target' and 'good to go' instead of naming the metric, so each person naturally maps the phrase onto their own standard; because both standards are normally correlated, neither has a reason to probe further.

misalignment_points.topic: Which snapshot is the latest baseline
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss comparing the new run against 'the latest baseline.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Leah means the September post-pruning-freeze training snapshot that matches the current sparse masks, codepath, and distributed launcher used for recent end-to-end system numbers.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun means the August sparse export used to generate the benchmark inputs and partition comparison tables in his latest analysis directory.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Each workstream has only one internally salient artifact that gets called 'the latest baseline,' and because the model family, sparsity target, and headline setup are the same, the version mismatch feels too minor to surface in a routine coordination exchange.

misalignment_points.topic: What belongs in the Master Results Sheet
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Leah will 'update the Master Results Sheet' after the run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Leah assumes this means entering not only throughput and communication numbers but also the experiment provenance needed to reproduce the run, including commit hash, partition checksum, reservation ID, and notes on how the partition artifact was prepared.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun assumes updating the Master Results Sheet means only adding the headline result rows, while partition-generation details and auxiliary provenance remain outside the sheet in his partition stats folder.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The Master Results Sheet is a familiar shared artifact whose name suggests completeness while also functioning as a dashboard, so both participants project their local norm onto it and hear the same phrase as settled routine admin.
